name: Avatar
purpose: Show who a person or a team is: their photo, or shared fallback artwork when there isn't one, with at most one presence or status badge.
intent: A compact, circular identity marker that sits beside person-related content, or acts as a button for picking or filtering by person.
nativeElement: span (role="img"), or button when isInteractive or onClick is set

apiAdaptationNotes: entityType has no corresponding Figma variant - added 2026-08-21 (re-verified against the avatar component set's own componentPropertyDefinitions, which only defines size/status/state/presence/isInteractive/isDisabled/selected - no team/entity axis) so Avatar's fallback artwork can distinguish an individual (the existing person silhouette) from a team/partner entity (a new two-person silhouette) when there is no src. The team silhouette is not invented art - it's the real, already-shipped team-and-partners icon glyph (packages/ui/src/assets/icons/source/team-and-partners.svg), rescaled and recolored to exactly match the person fallback's own template (a 200x200 flat-color square with a centered glyph, same two light/dark color pairs) rather than drawn from scratch.

useCases: The person on a record: an owner, a trustee, a beneficiary, an advisor
Who did something, in a comment, an activity feed, or an audit trail
Availability (presence) or a reply to an invitation (status)
A person people pick, as a button with isInteractive and isSelected
A team or partner firm among people, with entityType="team"
antiPatterns: A firm, trust, or account as its own primary identity marker
A general action (use Icon Button or Button)
More than one badge at once

anatomy.description: A span with role="img", or a native button when interactive. Owns size, data attributes, focus ring classes, and the accessible name.
The circle: the surface fill, the hover and press overlay (::after), and the selected ring (::before).
The image from src, or the light or dark fallback artwork for entityType when there's no usable image. Clipped to the circle.
Shown only with a presence or status: a disc in the surface color at the bottom-end corner that sets the badge off from the image.
The presence or status glyph inside the badge container, ringed with the inverse border color.

entityType.note: No Figma variant - see figmaSource.apiAdaptationNotes. Selects which fallback artwork renders when there is no src (or it fails to load).

accessibility.role: img on the static span; native button when interactive
accessibility.accessibleName: aria-labelledby, else aria-label, name, or alt, in that order. Avatar appends "selected" and the visible badge (online, offline, busy, accepted, declined) to a name from aria-label, name, or alt; nothing is appended with aria-labelledby.
accessibility.image: The img is alt="" and aria-hidden; the fallback artwork is aria-hidden.
accessibility.decorative: decorative hides a static avatar (aria-hidden, no role, no name). Ignored when interactive.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: In development, Avatar warns in the console when a non-decorative avatar has no accessible name.
accessibility.selection: Selection is announced only through "selected" in the name; the button doesn't set aria-pressed.
accessibility.focus: Shared Focus Ring on the interactive button, offset by --spacing-xxs.

keyboardInteraction: Tab moves focus to an interactive avatar; a disabled one is skipped
Enter and Space activate an interactive avatar (native button behavior)
behaviorRules: Render a native button when isInteractive is true or onClick is a function; otherwise a span with role="img".
The button defaults to type="button" and uses the native disabled attribute for isDisabled.
status takes precedence over presence; at most one badge renders.
An image that fails to load is replaced by the fallback artwork; a new src resets the failure and is tried again.
entityType selects the person or team fallback artwork and has no effect once an image loads.
isSelected draws an inset ring of --border-width-md in --color-border-brand-primary-default, on static and interactive avatars, and appends "selected" to the name.
isDisabled dims the avatar to 40% opacity and removes hover and press overlays.
Hover and press overlays apply only to an interactive, enabled avatar.
do: Give every meaningful avatar a name, even with a photo.
Let Avatar add selection and the badge to the accessible name.
Mark an avatar decorative when a visible name sits next to it.
dont: Rely on the photo alone for the name.
Write the presence or selection into name yourself.
Set decorative on an interactive avatar to drop its name.
Set presence and status together expecting both to show.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders a span with role="img" by default and a button when interactive.
Falls back to the entityType artwork without src or on image failure, and retries a new src.
Appends selected and badge state to the accessible name.
Decorative static avatars are hidden from assistive technology.
Disabled interactive avatars use the native disabled attribute.
Interactive avatars use the shared Focus Ring.
